description.purpose: The first hive with a domain of its own: the curated record of the people and agents a colony knows. Five cells, no model. `store` holds whole AIeOS 1.1.0 documents in an `aieos` column, everything meclaw adds beside them under `mx`, and the four things AIeOS has no vocabulary for as tables -- relations (cut exactly on the traverse signature), trust, disclosure and an append-only audit. `gate` is the only writer and the only place AIeOS conformance is decided. `brief` is the only reader and the only place the audience filter exists. `push` compares hashes and decides WHETHER a subscriber hears anything; `clock` ticks it. Memory produces, affinity decides -- and only affinity is quoted when the answer is `who is X to me`. 3.1.1 is a third-digit move by `docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a and nothing more: no lane moved, no column was added and no cell changed behaviour -- `push` already filtered on `status` and `gate` already wrote it. What changed is ONE VALUE in a seed row (`active` -> `inactive`) and the prose that described it. Since [#488](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/488) the record also holds the AGENT side of the same idea, and it costs no new cell and no new lane: `mx.brain` is a reserved subtree of an entity's own `mx` -- one object per `system.*` family, one raw text per leaf -- and `brief` grows a FIFTH request slot, `brain`, that reads it. The durable home of what an agent is and how it answers is therefore its own record here, and a brain's `system.*` tree is a delivered copy; because `entities.mx` is a `json` column of a table this hive already exports, the identity travels the transfer lane that already exists instead of needing a fifth holder or a change to `./porter`. Until then those slots lived only in a brain's own `cell.db`, nothing exported them and no template seeded them, so a colony rebuilt from its own export brought its agent up with an empty charter. The slot is a contract addition and not a behaviour change: a request that names no `slots` still gets the four person slots and never `brain`, and the version is untouched by it. Since 3.3.0 the export of the curated record is not a stack of messages any more ([#555](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/555)): the `store` writes its own `seed/<table>.jsonl` set through the substrate's `transfer` slot, inside the fence it declares in `params.transfer.base_path`, and `./porter` says `export_done` off the slot's own receipt. The walk ORDER stays here, because it is this hive's knowledge and load-bearing on the way in; what left is the reading. Since 3.3.0 the five behaviour knobs are PARAMS of the cells that read them rather than `${AFFINITY_*}` substitutions ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138)): `./brief` declares `disclosure_rows`, `traverse_depth` and `traverse_nodes`, `./push` declares `subscriber_rows`, and `./clock`'s cadence is a literal inside `params.schedules` -- each one a value under `params`, a declaration in `contract.settings` and, for the scripted four, a literal in the script, with the defaults unchanged. This hive reads no `.env` line at all now (it asks no provider anything), and two members of one colony keep their records at two cadences -- which an `override_params` entry can say precisely because the key exists under `params` (GH #294).
description.use_when: Once per family or org tree, as a sibling of the agents rather than inside one, because an agent's persona and a person's record are the same document in this hive and both are read by several agents. Wire the two ports in the same mutation as the add_nodes. The brief ingress MUST deliver the asker AND the round (`hop.audience` + `hop.audience_set`, which the door edge promotes to `context.asker` / `context.audience_set` -- or the same two keys promoted on the caller's own edge) and the propose ingress MUST promote the writer to `context.actor` and, for `subscribe`, the subscribing cell's address to `context.subscriber`: these cells take identity from the edge and never from body text, because a body is model-writable and an edge is not. Precedence at the door is edge-pinned first (`context.asker` -> `hop.audience` -> '' for the asker, `context.audience_set` -> `hop.audience_set` -> '' for the round), so a cell downstream of the pinning edge cannot shrink its own room by stamping a hop key. `context.participants` was this hive's internal name for the round until GH #330; it is retired, not aliased -- a request that declares its round only under the old name is refused `no_round`, and no template may ever introduce a second name for it. A request that declares no round at all is refused the same way (GH #306) -- reading it as the asker alone is the WIDEST reading a subset test can be given, not the narrowest. Identity references inside the round are affinity's alone to mint and map (UUID-backed here, byte-identical on the wire); receptionist, memory and talky only transport them and never resolve them. Since 3.2.0 the hive also carries a TRANSFER lane: `in_export` walks the record out as a versioned document, one `dump` part per table, and `in_import` takes one part back into a hive that is already running. Wire both drains (`dump` and `reject`) in the same mutation as the ingress -- `params.required_drains` refuses the mutation otherwise, because an export nobody takes is a walk that reaches nobody (GH #471). A self-subscription is how an agent's own identity gets back OUT to its brain: subscribe the agent to its own subject with `slots: ["brain"]` and wire the push edge into the composite's `in_pack` lane, whose closed list of families is the collector's `PACK_SLOTS` (`identity`, `persona`, `handover`, `instructions`). Two rules a caller meets there: `identity` and `brain` in ONE request are refused with `slots_conflict`, because the rendered person slot and an `mx.brain` `identity` family land on the same slot path and the rendered one would swallow every path under it; and `mx.brain` is a field path like any other, so without a `disclosure` row naming it for the asking audience the answer carries nothing at all.
description.not_in_scope: No LLM, and no human either: nothing in this hive reads a proposal in order to judge it. A memory-born proposal lands in `proposals` with status `accepted` and the actor the edge named as `decided_by` -- R-AF-1, because the safety net is the substrate rather than a queue somebody has to work through: no branch of `gate` ever emits `delete`, and a verdict appends instead of overwriting the row it judged. `auto_accept: false` is the exception a caller asks for deliberately; that row lands `open` and waits for a later `decide_proposal`. The seeded subscription ships INACTIVE and is an EXAMPLE of the shape rather than a live delivery (GH #458): a row is half a subscription, the other half is a push edge only a mutation may draw, so a subscription becomes live when a `subscribe` op stamps it -- the edge first, the row second, because an edge with no active row behind it carries nothing while a row with no edge behind it is silently undeliverable (GH #289). No name resolution (a subject is an entity_id), no per-turn recall (that stays the direct collector-to-memory wire) and no encryption at rest. And sovereignty is enforced only in half: the substrate refuses a write from outside the hive (`write_denied`, from the store's `write_surface: "internal"`) and refuses a mutation that names a path inside it (`hive_port_boundary`), but a parent's BOOT graph may wire straight into `./store` and a read from anywhere is free -- the audience filter lives in `./brief`, after the read. The audit table makes a bypass visible afterwards; nothing prevents it.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty; an edge naming ./brief, ./gate or ./push is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route. in_brief: an edge into the HIVE carrying the request as a tool_call turn ({subject, channel, slots}) plus the asker and the round on the hop (hop.audience, hop.audience_set), which the door edge promotes to context.asker and context.audience_set -- `participants` is retired, not aliased (GH #330), so a request that spells the round that way declared no round at all; a missing or unknown asker (no_audience) and an undeclared round (no_round) both get an answer with NO system slot at all; the door also resets aff_phase/aff_carry/aff_subscriber so a fresh request cannot inherit a lane. out_brief: the hive path on hop.route=='answer' && hop.subscriber=='' into the asking llm cell -- system.identity|peer|relationship|channel, each a renderable leaf -- or, for a request that asked for the `brain` slot (GH #488), one system.<family> per family of the subject's reserved mx.brain subtree, whose leaves are raw texts and are deliberately NOT rendered, -- plus a tool_result carrying the receipt line, that same pack as JSON (a sealed agent hive drops the system slot on its tool lane) and the id of the call being answered. in_propose: an edge into the HIVE on the write side, promoting the writer to context.actor and, for subscribe, the subscribing cell's address to context.subscriber -- the subscription row is an ADDRESS the hive's push lane reads every tick, so a body that names cell_path or audience is refused with identity_from_body (GH #288). out_ack: the hive path on hop.route=='ack' back to the proposer (accepted|rejected plus a reason_code). out_push: the hive path on hop.route=='answer' && hop.subscriber=='<cell path>' into each subscribed llm cell -- system.* and no turn beside it, so the slot update costs the subscriber a write and not an inference (GH #263). The parent draws ONE such edge per subscribing cell at instantiation and conditions it on that cell's own path: a subscribe writes a row, never an edge (mutation authority is the colony's), so a subscription with no edge behind it is accepted and undeliverable. The out_brief edge in the same graph MUST carry hop.subscriber=='' or it collects every push as well -- brief stamps subscriber on EVERY answer emission, the tool lane as the empty string, so the emptiness is a value and not an absence (GH #289). out_error: the hive path on hop.route=='error' into a drain the parent MUST wire.

attune once per agent birth: affinity_brief{subject:'entity:aiden'} over the boot lane -> system.identity from the AGENT's own AIeOS document, accumulated in the llm cell's cell.db per slot path; every slot carries a `text` rendering beside its structure, because an llm cell concatenates `text` leaves into the prompt and renders nothing else (GH #258)

a person the audience has three disclosure rows for -> exactly those three fields; the same person for an audience with no row -> the document is never even read, one audit row says denied, and the answer carries nothing
who is Sam to Alex: ONE traverse op over `relations`, two hops, answered by the store instead of by a graph walk in a script
a curated correction: gate marks the active row superseded and inserts the new one -- no delete is ever emitted, so the previous record stays readable

push-on-change: every tick hashes what each subscriber WOULD get; unchanged means zero messages, changed means exactly one re-brief through ./brief, so the audience filter can only be wrong in one place. seed/subscribers.jsonl ships ONE row -- the seeded agent's own document into the seeded agent's own brain, channel `*`, slot `identity` -- and since 3.1.1 it ships it INACTIVE (GH #458): the row ships no edge and cannot, writing one is a mutation, so an `active` seed claimed a delivery the shipped tree cannot make. `push` selects on status = 'active', so a fresh hive is silent because nothing has SUBSCRIBED -- which the `status` column states out loud, rather than being indistinguishable from unchanged data (GH #453). Its `cell_path` is a birth-state token like `entity:alex`, and the mutation that instantiates the MEMBER -- the owner of the subscription, which is the half GH #302 left open -- either conditions the push edge on that token or rewrites the row through ./gate

moving a person to a second colony: send `in_export` to the hive path, drain `export_done`, and the store writes the nine tables itself as `<fence>/<dir>/affinity/seed/<table>.jsonl` -- schema line first, one row per line after it, `export_final.json` last. Birth the new hive from those files and the trust rows, the disclosure decisions and the merge judgements are there before the first turn; `pack_hash` and `sent_at` are blanked on the way in, so the new colony still makes its own first identity-pack delivery
